title: Precision affinity profiles and runtime fallback handshake for mixed-precision dispatch
creator: Asha Raman
description: Implement a precision-affinity profile layer and a deterministic runtime fallback handshake that lets the serving runtime select per-request/per-layer kernels across FP16/FP8/INT8 execution paths while preserving accuracy SLOs. This ticket covers the runtime-side policy, lightweight metadata formats for quant profiles, integration points for offline calibration artifacts, and a canary rollout for the fallback policies.
tasks: Design a precision-affinity profile format (compact JSON + proto) that encodes per-layer candidate precisions, estimated token-cost, and expected accuracy delta
Extend the runtime kernel registry to accept affinity hints and a ‘handshake’ API between scheduler and kernel to negotiate fallback at dispatch time
Add support for deterministic calibration seeds and per-channel scale tables ingestion from calibration artifacts produced by the calibration pipeline
Implement a lightweight online accuracy probe that samples 0.1% of requests for full-precision verification when fallback to lower precision is used
Create a canary rollout flow in Console: traffic weighting, rollback thresholds, and metric dashboards (latency, token-cost, accuracy-probe delta)
End-to-end tests: microbenchmarks for latency/cost, and an evaluation harness running representative prompts comparing FP16 baseline vs mixed-precision path
Documentation: runtime API changes, suggested calibration artifact schema, and Ops runbook for troubleshooting fallback-induced regressions
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can accept a precision-affinity profile artifact and choose kernel paths without requiring model graph changes
Fallback handshake ensures deterministic decision given the same request and runtime state (no race-based nondeterminism)
Canary rollout tooling exposes: per-route accuracy delta, per-token cost reduction, and tail latency change; alerts if accuracy-probe delta > 1.5% absolute on critical prompts

Integration tests show <2% average quality regression (measured by cosine similarity on embedding retention and ROUGE-L on text tasks) for mixed-precision compared to FP16 baseline under calibrated profiles
Calibration artifacts (scale tables) are versioned and auditable; runtime logs include artifact id used per-request for traceability
comments: 2026-03-10 — Kickoff: scoped with Prod and Research. Agreed to start with a compact affinity JSON to avoid proto churn; final storage will be artifact-bundled in model registry. (Asha)

2026-03-11 — Engineering spike: Miguel prototyped handshake path. Observed 8% token-cost reduction on small Llama-variant with naive FP8 first policy, but a handful of prompts showed grammatical artifacts. Decided to add online accuracy probe. (Miguel)

2026-03-11 — Research note: calibration pipeline will produce both histogram-min-MSE scale tables and per-layer activation distributions. We prefer MSE-min for INT8 and per-channel symmetric for FP8 experiments. (Dr. Lin)

2026-03-12 — Design decision: handshake must be stateless from scheduler perspective and carry a fallback vector; kernel will return a deterministic failure code if numeric instability detected so scheduler can move to next candidate. Added backlog item for kernel-side failure codes. (Asha)
